problem_statement:
OSTest exposes a work-queue correctness problem when work is queued and cancelled under contention from threads of various priorities. The added test in apps/testing/ostest/wqueue.c is built when CONFIG_SCHED_WORKQUEUE is set and uses LPWORK or HPWORK (CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORK / CONFIG_SCHED_HPWORK). It is invoked from ostest as wqueue_test.

The test has two phases. The first phase runs a tester thread that repeatedly performs up to 100 iterations of work_queue() followed immediately by work_cancel() for the same struct work_s. The tester uses a 0 or 1 microsecond interval and runs at priorities one below, equal to, or one above the configured work-queue priority. The second phase runs a verifier that queues a long-running sleep work item and then queues 100 short count work items. After the sleep item completes, the verifier waits and expects all 100 count work items to have been executed exactly once, with every struct work_s cleared.

With the current kernel, this test can fail with an assertion in wqueue_test, or ostest can fail before printing 'user_main: Exiting'. The failure indicates that the work queue has become unusable or inconsistent after rapid queue/cancel activity. The most problematic case is when a work item is queued and then cancelled from a higher-priority context before the work queue has serviced that item, but the test also exercises same and lower priority cases. Observable symptoms include later queued work not being dispatched, incorrect completion counts, or work items still marked as pending after the queue should have become idle.

The required behavior is that work_queue() and work_cancel() must remain correct under priority-induced races: cancellation of queued work must not leave the queue in a state where subsequent queued work is dropped or not serviced, and queued work must ultimately be executed exactly once. The added wqueue_test should complete successfully for LPWORK/HPWORK configurations after the kernel is fixed.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: On a work queue, a high-priority task that repeatedly queues a work item and immediately cancels it in a tight loop can drive the work-queue semaphore count to a large negative value, and the work_thread only processes a single item per wake. As a result, work items queued while the queue is in this inconsistent state are not triggered, so not all queued workers run. The test must verify that after such stressing the queue remains consistent: all 100 queued count workers run exactly once (call_count == VERIFY_COUNT) and all work entries are cleared (work[i].worker == NULL).
check_issues: `problem_statement` gives the fix away: "can drive the work-queue semaphore count to a large negative value"; "the work_thread only processes a single item per wake"; "work items queued while the queue is in this inconsistent state are not triggered". Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally
